quality_check.description: A single vertical atlas-card image with a thick imperfect soot-black outer border, narrow bone-white margin, and inset illustration window. A large blue-gray circular band is populated by many repeated white swan silhouettes. At the lower-left edge, a solid black swan breaks through the ring amid sharp pale angular fragments and a sparse vermilion rupture. Thin circular, radial, and fractured construction lines surround the symbol. The image uses matte bone-white, pale stone, storm blue-gray, black, and restrained vermilion with visible archival grain and worn print character.
violations: The circular rule-symbol is not constructed entirely from repeated white swan silhouettes because the swans sit on a substantial continuous blue-gray annular band.

Technical geometry around the ring is more abundant and visually prominent than the requested limited treatment, including multiple concentric arcs and several long radial or diagonal construction lines.

The lower portion of the illustration window becomes comparatively sparse and low-detail, with a large pale-stone field rather than maintaining similarly active scene texture through the full usable height.
Restrained oxidized teal is not clearly visible as a distinct palette accent.
The rupture fragments and surrounding geometry spread somewhat broadly beyond the immediate impact point, making the transition cue less singular and concentrated than requested.

prompt:
Edit

Create exactly one 9:16 image in a fractured-probability screen-print style: dry matte ink, coarse archival grain, slight registration wear, bold soot-black contours, bone-white and pale-stone grounds, muted storm blue-gray and restrained oxidized teal, with vermilion used only for the rupture. Inside the recurring vertical atlas-card frame—thick imperfect soot-black outer print edge, narrow bone-white margin, inset rectangular illustration window with worn corners—show a large centered circular rule-symbol constructed entirely from repeated white swan silhouettes, orderly enough to feel universal and certain. At the lower-left edge, one solid black swan forcefully breaks through the ring, splitting the circle into sharp angular fragments; trace only a sparse vermilion crack through the break to emphasize the single contradictory observation. Use graphic high-contrast matte light fields and deep ink shadows, with subtle thin technical geometry around the ring that fractures and diverges at the impact point. Fill the complete illustration height naturally; do not reserve any lower caption field, blank strip, empty panel, or low-detail band. Reference roles: style_reference governs the simplified screen-print medium and treatment; world_keyframe establishes the recurring atlas-card world, palette, texture, and graphic lighting; previous_beat is binding only for frame language, material/edge treatment, inner window, texture, palette, lighting, and full-height caption layout—do not copy its composition, crop, camera angle, subject placement, or focal object. No photorealism, glossy 3D, anime, watercolor, sepia engraving, neon cyberpunk, readable charts, interfaces, labels, letters, numbers, captions, or embedded text. Exactly one image only; no storyboard, grid, collage, or panels.

Clarify the transition cue visually
Limit technical geometry around the ring NON-NEGOTIABLE EPISODE FRAME CONTRACT: Preserve this recurring frame language in this image: every image appears inside the same vertically oriented screen-printed atlas card: a thick imperfect soot-black outer print edge, narrow bone-white breathing margin, and a slightly inset rectangular illustration window with tiny registration offsets and worn ink corners. Diagrams, environments, swans, tools, markets, and technology scenes all remain inside this repeated print-window grammar, with the border thickness and inner margins held consistent throughout the episode. Preserve its material/edge grammar, texture, palette and inner illustration window while changing only the scene inside it. Do not reserve a lower caption field, blank strip, empty panel or low-detail band. Continue the scene and its natural texture through the full usable height, guided by the previous accepted image, without adding text, letters, numbers, captions, labels, words or UI.
